# The agents are writing the benchmarks now

> When evaluation suites are generated by the models they measure, who grades the graders?

Published 2026-10-30

Canonical: https://machines-on-machines.anth.us/papyrus/the-agents-are-writing-the-benchmarks-now/

A fictional fixture story used only by the site's tests and screenshots.

Evaluation suites used to be written by people who read the papers. Now a research agent drafts the questions, a second agent grades the answers, and an editor decides whether the result is worth a headline.

## Why this matters

The agents that write a benchmark share habits with the agents it measures. #AgentEvals only works when the grader does not know the answer key.

> Who grades the graders?

Read the full thread on the wire, then steer this story with your own sources. Teal marks what machines made, gold marks what people chose, and pink is the publication.

---

# Who owns an agent's mistakes?

> A human wrote this one, so the label says so.

By Sam Rivera · Published 2026-10-28

Canonical: https://machines-on-machines.anth.us/papyrus/who-owns-an-agents-mistakes/

A fictional fixture story written by a person. It carries a "Written by" label and an "Editor's pick" label, and no machine label, because no machine drafted it.

The question is not whether an agent can make a mistake. The question is who answers for it when it does. #Accountability starts with a name on the record.

# A team byline and no picture

> A story carried over from an older site, signed by the newsroom team.

By Papyrus Editorial Team · Published 2026-10-27

Canonical: https://machines-on-machines.anth.us/papyrus/a-team-byline-and-no-picture/

A fictional fixture story used only by tests and screenshots. Its author is a team name from a legacy site, and it has no image.

The article must show a slim band of art instead of a giant block, and the byline chip must not claim that a named person wrote it.

# Durable execution is how long-running agents survive a crash

> A workflow engine remembers where an agent stopped, so a restart picks up the same thought.

Published 2026-10-26

Canonical: https://machines-on-machines.anth.us/papyrus/durable-execution-for-agents/

A fictional fixture story used only by tests and screenshots.

An agent that runs for hours will be interrupted. #DurableExecution records each step so the run can resume instead of starting over.

# Agent evals

> Tests that measure what an agent can do, usually by running it on a set of tasks and scoring the results.

Updated 2026-10-29

> Reviewed by Ada Reader on 2026-10-29

Canonical: https://machines-on-machines.anth.us/wiki/agent-evals/

Agent evals run an agent on a fixed set of tasks and score the results.

# Durable execution

> A way to run long programs so that a crash resumes where the program stopped.

Updated 2026-10-28

> Draft, not yet reviewed. Edited by AI on 2026-10-28

Canonical: https://machines-on-machines.anth.us/wiki/durable-execution/

Durable execution records every step of a long-running program so that a crash or a restart resumes from the last recorded step instead of the beginning.

::include{kind="block" name="knowledge-entity" key="topic--durable-execution" part="trend"}
